title: Vodnjan
eyebrow: Dignano · five generations · read by eye from a book no index contains
dek: Twelve families in a 1945 cadastre, and nothing behind them. Then the parish books were opened.
lead:
For most of this archive's life Vodnjan was a number: **twelve Defranceschi families in the 1945 cadastre**, more than anywhere else in Istria, and not one line of descent to attach them to. It was listed as the second open question.

On **9 and 10 September 2026** the parish books were read. The baptism register is indexed; **the marriage register is indexed nowhere on earth**, and was read opening by opening, by eye. What follows came out of it.

Everything below is transcribed from the page. Where a join is inferred rather than written, it says so.

open.heading: What is still open, stated as open
rows: Two Stefani, or one man twice married

The index has **Stefano De Franceschi × Maria Francin** baptising five children 1854–1865, and **Stefano De Franceschi × Maria Forlanichio** baptising two in 1858 and 1860. The years **overlap**, which normally settles it — two men. But *Forlanichio* and *Francin* are close enough on a page that one clerk's hand could produce both, and the 1858 births fall four months apart, which a single household cannot do. **Either there are two Stefani, or the index has split one man's wife into two women.** The Vodnjan marriage register for the 1850s decides it; that film has not been opened.

Lucia Michiela De Franceschi bore four Forlani children 1848–1857, so she was born around 1825. **Two Lucias fit**: the one baptised **25 July 1826** to Gio. Maria and Lucia Bonassin, and the one baptised **25 August 1828** to Pietro and Maddalena Francin. Both are in this archive; neither can be preferred. A marriage entry naming her father would end it in one line.
Whether the four lines are one

Vodnjan has now produced **four** De Franceschi lines that this archive keeps separate: **Gio. Maria's**, **Giuseppe's**, **Domenico's** (the Cerlon household) and **Pietro → Domenico → Stefano** at house 325. Every one of them has a **Pietro** at or near the top. That is either a family that reused one forename for four generations — which is exactly what this parish does — or four branches of one house. **The dispensation files of the Ordinariate of Pola would say outright**, because a dispensation states the degree of kinship; this archive cannot.
Four Pietros, and how many men that really is

The register has produced **Pietro q.m Gio: Maria** (b. c.1776), **Pietro di Giuseppe** the ploughman, **Pietro di Gio.** the weaver, **Pietro q.m Pietro** the ploughman of the second line, and a **Pietro × Martina Civico** whose son Domenico married in 1832. Some of these may be one man. The register settles it only when it chooses to write a patronymic, and it does not always choose.
**Cristoforo *fu Gio: Maria***, agricoltore, and **Cristoforo *di Giuseppe***, tessitore, alive in the same town in the same year. Only the father's name separates them.

They share a town, a surname and a handful of forenames. **That is not evidence.** The place to settle it is the dispensation files of the Ordinariate of Pola, which this register cites by protocol number and which would state the degree of kinship outright.

Lucia Tromba is the mother of Don Stefano; Giovanni Tromba is the parson who licensed him. In a town this size that is very likely kin — and it is **inferred from a shared surname**, which is exactly the reasoning this archive distrusts everywhere else.

source: Vodnjan (Dignano), Liber Baptizatorum and Liber Copulatorum in Ecclesia S. Blasii — FamilySearch catalogue koha:963267, DGS 005497893 and 005497894. Marriages read image by image, 172–216, on 9–10 September 2026. The marriage register is not indexed by FamilySearch: 286 marriage-query arks were resolved against film 894 and none is on it.

houses.heading: The house numbers, and the one that repeats
houses.lead:
Every entry in these books carries a **№ domus**. It is the most under-used column in the whole register — and it is the only field that can join two households when the names refuse to.

**One caution that removes most of the list.** The house number belongs to **the couple being married or the person who died**, not to the witnesses. So the twenty-odd numbers standing against Don Stefano's name are other people's houses, and they prove nothing about his. What follows is only the entries where the number is the subject's own.

houses.note:
**House 325 belongs to Stefano De Franceschi and Bonetta Vellico.** Their daughter Maria died there in March 1829 and Bonetta herself in September 1830, and her entry writes the husband out three deep: «Stefano De Franceschi ***di*** Domenico ***q.m*** Pietro» — father living, grandfather dead.

That matters because the same number stands against **Domenico De Franceschi, forty-six, son of a Pietro and Martina Civico**, remarrying as a widower in July 1832. Two households, one house, and now a shared grandfather's name.

**The connection is likely; which connection is open.** On the stated ages the 1832 Domenico, born about 1786, is too young to be Stefano's father — so it is two brothers of one name, an uncle, or an age the register got wrong. Vodnjan also renumbered its houses more than once. **A house number is a thread, not a proof**, and this one is recorded so the next reader tests it rather than rediscovers it.

Note also **324**, next door: that is **Giuseppe De Franceschi's** house, where he died on 14 February 1830 and out of which his daughter Maria Francesca married in 1833. *(doc for every number; every connection drawn from them is **open**)*
